---
title: "Layout and execution"
---

## One modeled system, several distinct lifetimes

Biology can constrain computation because repeated model evaluations often
share entities, relations, and structural organization. A coherent runtime
must preserve those identities while deciding which work is active and how
to represent it on hardware. Keep these responsibilities explicit:

```text
identity and structure
        ↓
activity and eligible work
        ↓
physical layout and index maps
        ↓
prepared operation and reusable resources
        ↓
runtime bindings and execution
```

The diagram describes distinct concepts, not a claim that every current
operation passes through one universal pipeline. Each facility defines its
own implemented boundary and maturity.

## Identity, support, routing, gating

Identity records which modeled entities and relation occurrences are meant.
Support describes which parts are eligible for an operation or evaluation.
Indexing gives efficient lookup; routing maps eligible work to an operation
or mechanism; gating controls conditional work. These concepts can cooperate
without collapsing into a single sparse matrix or dispatcher. Structure epochs
and value generations must remain distinct when their invalidation behavior
differs.

Cellerator has early implementations in sparse support, ordered indexing,
routing, and gating. Their measurements and tests cover particular contracts
and workloads. A selected sparse path must preserve identity and define
overflow, capacity, stale-structure, update, and derivative behavior. It is
not automatically better than dense execution, and measured indexing gains do
not imply an end-to-end model speedup.

The opt-in prepared entity-to-mechanism route query uses caller-supplied
identity and generation values to decide whether its reverse-posting index can
be reused. It emits a query result for the existing discrete route policy; it
does not learn or reinterpret routes. The frozen binary passed exact CUDA
correctness and memcheck, racecheck, and synccheck. A bounded V100 lifecycle
measurement showed a long-reuse win for one synthetic ranked input shape, an
inconclusive event result, and losses to dense Torch on larger stress shapes.
The prepared strategy remains opt-in. See the
[source-bound report](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/94c534fc794fe8cc3e0434e4a50f379401ddbb3c/bench/sparse_support/experiments/prepared_routing/REPORT.md)
for the cold-cost, workload, and comparison limits. This is an operation-
specific example of explicit preparation identity, not a package-wide adaptive
dispatcher.

## Layout and execution

Layout is the physical mapping of logical values and derivatives. Execution
defines preparation, reuse, allocation, stream and device bindings, and the
actual lifetime of executable work. A structure discovery result is not a
physical layout; a layout candidate is not a runtime resource; and neither is
evidence of adaptation by itself.

The architecture preserves several runtime requirements: biological domain
and order identity are stable; structure epochs are separate from mutable
value generations; runtime gates should be established before execution when
possible; complete setup, conversion, allocation, synchronization, and
execution costs matter; and candidate selection is measured rather than
mandated by one sparse format or accelerator route. These are design
contracts, not evidence that all operations implement adaptive execution.

## Fields and compilation

Execution fields and compiler/IR work are experimental. The current
`ExecutionField` composes a prepared native Product2 Torch module, uses CPU
FP32 rank-one inputs, and exposes explicit immutable stage structure, structure
epoch, value/binding generation, and `rebind_structure`. It has five installed
CPU tests reported passing. It does not provide JIT compilation, GPU dispatch,
or live recompilation. See [experimental fields](development/experimental-fields.md)
for its narrow contract and limitations.

Compilation may eventually help generate and validate execution plans, much
as TorchScript historically relates to Torch modules, but ordinary Cellerator
operations must not depend on a compiler runtime. Live recompilation is not a
stable package promise. See [experiments and history](experiments_and_history.qmd)
for legacy compiler docs and preserved evidence.

## Evidence boundary

Do not infer a performance claim from source presence, an execution graph, a
sparse representation, or a microbenchmark. Report the workload, hardware,
setup and conversion costs, numerical checks, repeated-use assumptions, and
excluded regions. The [performance and validation guide](performance_validation.qmd)
defines this evidence boundary; the dated [implementation record](current_implementation.qmd)
links current results.
